title: Sickle cell gene therapy access and durability
bottleneck: CRISPR-based Casgevy and lentiviral Lyfgenia can functionally cure sickle cell disease, but each treatment costs millions, requires myeloablative conditioning with infertility and malignancy risks, and is available at only a handful of centers, inaccessible to most of the millions affected, largely in sub-Saharan Africa.
why_it_blocks: A cure that cannot reach the population bearing the disease burden is a scientific success and a delivery failure.
current_state: Uptake has been limited even in wealthy countries, with approved gene therapies seeing little use; in vivo editing that avoids conditioning and manufacturing bottlenecks is the hoped-for next step. Long-term durability data are still maturing. In vivo editing approaches that avoid myeloablative conditioning could dramatically expand access, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa where the disease burden is highest. Until then, the gap between curative science and reachable cure will persist.
